question: Should OpenClaw adopt this always-on durable voice-session and spoken-confirmation design as a core Talk contract after preserving existing generated client API compatibility?
rationale: The PR introduces persistent per-agent call state, new public RPCs, and behavior that changes how voice-originated tool actions execute; this is a product and compatibility decision beyond a mechanical review fix.

options.title: Sponsor the core direction
options.body: Accept durable voice sessions as a core Talk feature, require the Swift compatibility repair and real cross-client behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Land only an explicitly agreed minimal protocol and persistence slice, leaving confirmation and digest behavior for follow-up work.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers choose a broader Talk-session product direction and ownership model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core direction
recommendation.body: Accept durable voice sessions as a core Talk feature, require the Swift compatibility repair and real cross-client behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch and design proposal are authored in this Talk area, making this the strongest available routing candidate from the supplied evidence.
